text:
samira: FYI ran into a subtle UX problem with the Go Generator when we try to "gracefully stop" a long-lived streaming job. Repro in sampleapp/generator/drain-stop.go. Thoughts?

jon: what's the symptom? goroutine leak, duped output, or hang on Close()?

samira: hang on Close(). Caller does ctx cancel after persisting progress; SDK tries to drain inflight events for a bit but if auth refresh happens we race and Close blocks forever.

priya: quick sketch of our current pattern: we rely only on ctx cancel + stream.Close(), which is ambiguous. Maybe we need explicit Drain/ForceClose separation.

alan: agree. For long-lived generators apps want: 1) signal "finish delivering what you've already received" (drain), 2) timeout if drain takes too long, 3) force close immediately. Suggest API: `Stop(ctx, opts...)` where opts include WithTimeout and WithForce. But in Go ergonomic terms `StopGracefully(timeout time.Duration)` + `ForceClose()` is simpler.

samira: example I prototyped:
```go
// consumer
if err := stream.StopGracefully(5 * time.Second); err != nil {
  // fallback to force
  _ = stream.ForceClose()
}
```

jon: implementation notes: StopGracefully should cancel an internal reader->deliver goroutine only after a heartbeat ensures transport isn't mid-reconnect. Use internal transportCtx and a deliver queue with backpressure. Do not close delivery channel from both reader and Stop path.

priya: also add an explicit DrainComplete event so callers know the stream finished cleanly vs timed out. That reduces guesswork instead of checking Err() for context.Canceled.

alan: on dedupe: if we support resume later, advise apps to persist lastSequenceID and accept that Resume may replay the last event. Add Event.SequenceID and a Dedup example in sampleapp.

samira: CI saw a flaky: generator_drain_timeout_test failing 3/20. I filed https://ci/internal/stream-drain-213. Will add a deterministic test that simulates auth expiry during drain to validate ForceClose path.

ci-bot: :robot_face: nightly: generator_drain_timeout_test flaky; logs https://ci/internal/stream-drain-213/logs.

jon: small-term patch: implement StopGracefully that cancels a delivery context, waits on an ack channel with timeout, and then sets an `abandoned` atomic to prevent resumed transports from writing to the deliverychan. Should fix hangs.

priya: ergonomics note: avoid making StopGracefully require passing the caller ctx to the SDK; keep it a method on the stream that accepts a timeout so users don't accidentally cancel their overall operation context. That reduces onboarding friction.

alan: I'll draft a one-pager to align Node/Python semantics: Drain vs Abort vs ForceClose and whether resume is implicit. We should aim for parity where semantics translate (explicit drain/abort primitives).

samira: action items: jon -> PR for StopGracefully + ForceClose and fix double-close bug; priya -> update sampleapp/generator/drain-stop.go with dedupe + usage; alan -> parity doc and sequence_id spec; I'll add the deterministic test and link it in the PR.

samira: thanks team — this UX will save users from weird hangs when they try to persist progress and stop a job. :thumbsup:
